en: A farm that got picked up and moved because **the volcano kept aiming at it** — and the flood that did it is recorded almost hour by hour.

ctx: fact bullet — tour 7.0 / Fellsfjara → Vík 2 hour drive folks / 🏚️ Höfðabrekka
en: **Höfðabrekka** stood on the low ground below this slope. On **3 November 1660** Katla's flood reached it — *"kom fram að Höfðabrekku jöklagangur með ofurmáta miklum vatnsþunga"* — and on the **8th–9th of November** the biggest wave *"sópaði burtu kirkju og bæjarhúsum að mestu"*: **it took the church and most of the farm buildings.**

ctx: fact bullet — tour 7.0 / Fellsfjara → Vík 2 hour drive folks / 🏚️ Höfðabrekka
en: They rebuilt it **up on the ridge itself** — where it still is, and where you are looking. The farm kept its name and changed its address.

ctx: fact bullet — tour 7.0 / Fellsfjara → Vík 2 hour drive folks / 🏚️ Höfðabrekka
en: That is the pattern along this whole coast, and it is worth naming: people here do not abandon a place, they **move it upslope and carry on.**

ctx: fact bullet — tour 7.0 / Fellsfjara → Vík 2 hour drive folks / 🏚️ Höfðabrekka
en: Everything between here and the sea is the reason — **Mýrdalssandur**, a black plain that exists because Katla has repeatedly emptied a glacier across it.

ctx: the spoken close — tour 7.0 / Fellsfjara → Vík 2 hour drive folks / 🧊 Sveinn Pálsson
en: He worked out how glaciers move while riding between farms in this weather — and the world got round to reading it in 1945.

ctx: opening hook line — tour 7.0 / Fellsfjara → Vík 2 hour drive folks / 🧊 Sveinn Pálsson
en: In **1794** a country doctor stood in front of a glacier tongue and worked out something nobody in Europe had: **glaciers flow.** They are not frozen still. **They move like something thick and half-melted** — and he was about a century early.

ctx: fact bullet — tour 7.0 / Fellsfjara → Vík 2 hour drive folks / 🧊 Sveinn Pálsson
en: **Sveinn Pálsson**, **1762–1840.** He took a **natural-sciences degree in Copenhagen in the spring of 1791** — the first person in Denmark to sit that exam — and went home meaning to come back and finish the medical half. He never did finish it. He doctored anyway, for the rest of his life.

ctx: fact bullet — tour 7.0 / Fellsfjara → Vík 2 hour drive folks / 🧊 Sveinn Pálsson
en: In **1799** a new medical district was created covering **Árnessýsla, Rangárvallasýsla, Vestur-Skaftafellssýsla and the Westman Islands.** He took it up in **1800**, moved to **Suður-Vík in Mýrdalur in 1809** — the village we are driving into — and stayed there until he died in **1840.**

ctx: fact bullet — tour 7.0 / Fellsfjara → Vík 2 hour drive folks / 🧊 Sveinn Pálsson
en: The glaciers were his own time, not the job. At **Kvíárjökull in 1794** he looked at the curved cracks running across the ice and wrote that it had moved *"hálfbráðinn eða sem þykkt seigfljótandi efni"* — **half-melted, like a thick viscous substance.** That is the modern answer: ice deforms under its own weight and creeps downhill.

ctx: fact bullet — tour 7.0 / Fellsfjara → Vík 2 hour drive folks / 🧊 Sveinn Pálsson
en: Europe never got to read it. His ***Ferðabók*** and the glacier treatise ***Jöklaritið*** **stayed in manuscript and were not printed until 1945**, translated by **Jón Eyþórsson, Pálmi Hannesson and Steindór Steindórsson**; the English edition came in **2004.** By 1945 the credit for glacier flow had long gone elsewhere.

ctx: fact bullet — tour 7.0 / Fellsfjara → Vík 2 hour drive folks / 🧊 Sveinn Pálsson
en: And be accurate about the one guides get wrong: **he was not Iceland's first doctor.** That was his father-in-law, **Bjarni Pálsson**, the first *landlæknir*. Sveinn stood in as acting *landlæknir* himself, briefly, in **1803–04.**
